page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-96-highlssd is a memory-optimized and storage-oriented virtual machine built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 96 dedicated virtual CPUs and a total system memory of 756.0 GB, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include any GPU hardware accelerators and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Although the local storage size is designated as None in the system specifications, the platform utilizes NVMe SSD storage technology. This configuration delivers high memory density relative to the processing core count, making it a resource-dense option for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without the overhead of GPU acceleration. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is defined by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, which ensures predictable execution times for enterprise workloads.

This server type is designed for memory-intensive applications, large-scale databases, in-memory analytics, and enterprise resource planning systems. The combination of 96 dedicated vCPUs and 756.0 GB of RAM supports heavy concurrent processing and large working datasets, making it suitable for relational database management systems and structured data warehousing.
